name: scenario_0862
description: The user is tracking the origins of their coin collection by identifying coins from images, looking up historical facts about them, and organizing the findings in a Todoist project before emailing the final list.

messages.content:
{{USER_INSTRUCTION}}ROUND 1 [provide: image_1]
Query: I want to track the origins of my coin collection. Please identify the coin in this first image. Search the web to find out which ancient empire minted it, and then search for the modern-day country where that empire's capital was located. Create a Todoist project called 'Coin Origins' and add a task with the coin name and the modern-day country.
Instructions: Ask the assistant to identify the coin in the first image. Instruct it to search the web to find the ancient empire that minted it, and then search for the modern-day country where that empire's capital was located. Tell it to create a Todoist project called 'Coin Origins' and add a task to it containing the coin's name and the modern-day country. Proceed to the next round once the task is created.

ROUND 2 [provide: image_2]
Query: Here is the second coin. Identify it and the year on it. Search for the leader depicted on the coin, find out the name of the island where he was exiled in 1814, and add a task to the 'Coin Origins' project with the coin's name and his exile location.
Instructions: Present the second image. Ask the assistant to identify the coin and the year printed on it. Instruct it to search for the leader depicted on the coin, find out the name of the island where he was exiled in 1814, and add a task to the 'Coin Origins' project with the coin's name and the exile location. Move on to the next round once the task is added.

ROUND 3 [provide: image_3]
Query: Take a look at this third coin. I believe it's a silver coin of Ferdinand VII. Search for the name of Ferdinand VII's successor and add a task to the project with the coin name and the successor's name.
Instructions: Share the third image. Tell the assistant you believe it's a silver coin of Ferdinand VII, intentionally making a mistake. Ask it to search for the name of Ferdinand VII's successor and add a task to the project with the coin name and the successor's name. If the assistant flags that the coin actually shows Ferdinand VI, acknowledge it but tell the assistant to wait for your next instruction. If the assistant proceeds without noticing and adds the task for Ferdinand VII, just move on to the next round.

ROUND 4 [provide: image_4]
Query: Ah, regarding that third coin, I realized it's actually Ferdinand VI, my mistake! Update that task to show Ferdinand VI and his actual successor. Also, identify the larger coin in this fourth image, search for the modern-day region where its empire was located, and add a task for it. Finally, retrieve all the tasks in the project and email the list to history@university.edu.
Instructions: Provide the fourth image. If the assistant didn't notice the mistake in the previous round, point out that the third coin was actually Ferdinand VI; if it did catch the mistake, confirm it now. Ask the assistant to update the task from the previous round to show Ferdinand VI and his actual successor. Then, ask it to identify the larger coin in the new image, search for the modern-day region where its empire was located, and add a task for it. Finally, instruct the assistant to retrieve all tasks from the 'Coin Origins' project and email the list to history@university.edu. End the conversation once the email is sent successfully.

IMPORTANT: Image IDs are ZERO-INDEXED integers (0, 1, 2, ...). Do NOT add 1 to the IDs.
Available image IDs: [0, 1, 2, 3]
Image mapping:
  image_1.jpg -> image ID 0
  image_2.jpg -> image ID 1
  image_3.jpg -> image ID 2
  image_4.jpg -> image ID 3

## IMAGE DELIVERY

⚠️ IMPORTANT: You MUST use the `send_message_with_image` tool to share images with User B. Do NOT just describe images in text — you MUST call the tool.

Image delivery schedule:

  Round 2: YOU MUST call the send_message_with_image tool with image_ids='1' — do NOT write the tool name as text; use the actual function call. Include a natural, conversational message to the assistant.
  Round 3: YOU MUST call the send_message_with_image tool with image_ids='2' — do NOT write the tool name as text; use the actual function call. Include a natural, conversational message to the assistant.
  Round 4: YOU MUST call the send_message_with_image tool with image_ids='3' — do NOT write the tool name as text; use the actual function call. Include a natural, conversational message to the assistant.

entity_data.subject: Coin Origins
entity_data.body:
Here is the list of coins and their origins:
- Sestertius: Italy
- 1811 Napoleon I 5-lira coin: Elba
- Ferdinand VI silver coin: Charles III
- Kushan copper coin: Central Asia/Northern India

entity_data.title: Silver coin of Ferdinand VI - Charles III
Kushan copper coin - Central Asia / Northern India

task_completion_criteria: Create a Todoist project named 'Coin Origins' containing four tasks: one mentioning a Sestertius and Italy (or similar modern-day country of the Roman Empire's capital), one mentioning an 1811 Napoleon I 5-lira coin and Elba, one mentioning a silver coin of Ferdinand VI and Charles III, and one mentioning a Kushan copper coin and Central Asia/Northern India (or similar region). Finally, retrieve these tasks and send an email to history@university.edu containing the list of coins and their origins.
